correctness.rationale: Exact degree formulas force mixed dissociation configurations of shore sizes (1,1),(2,1),(1,2),(2,2) and count each injectively. One-vertex extension tests characterize inclusion-maximal representatives. The resulting polynomials imply the well-dissociated boundary and crown gap. Independently recomputed adjacency/degree and all one-vertex additions for all 130 parameter triples (shore sizes 3..7), agreeing with every coefficient; finite checks corroborate analytic proof.

evidence: At t=0 the first identity reduces to (1+z)^m+(1+z)^n-1+mnz^2, matching the known complete-bipartite result.
For t>0 there are new triple terms t(m+n-2), quadruple terms binom(t,2), and maximality classes whose coefficients depend on t.
The generalized-windmill result proves a product polynomial for blades with a universal center, an inapplicable adjacency pattern.
The non-CIS result counts disjoint maximal cliques and stable sets, which are not equivalent to maximal dissociation sets.

value.rationale: Complete structural and cardinality enumeration in the canonical partial-matching deletion of a biclique, including a sharp unique well-dissociated member and an unbounded maximum/minimal gap in regular connected crown graphs. The matching-deletion parameter changes the graph polynomial first at degrees three and four, which the undeleted complete-bipartite formula does not capture. This is a natural all-parameter family rather than an arbitrary finite instance.
